question: What happens to the motion of the particles as temperature rises?

options.text: The particles move in the same direction

solution:
The correct answer is __**The particles move faster**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A**s the temperature rises, the particles of matter move faster.**
 
• This is **because the particles gain kinetic energy**
 
• **Kinetic Energy** is the energy that a body possesses due to its motion.
 
• It is **directly proportional to both the mass of the body and the square of its velocity.**
 
• The mathematical expression for kinetic energy is:Kinetic Energy(KE)= 1/2 ​ mv²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When the temperature increases-
 
 
• **The particles gain kinetic energy and start vibrating.**
 
• **The particles move faster and take up more space.**
 
• **The forces of attraction between the particles weaken.**
 
• **This can lead to a change in the state of matter.**
